source_meta._title: Renamed minecarts and boats don't show their name tag in the world

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.17.1 in a vanilla single-player Creative Mode world. Use an open, flat area with enough unobstructed space to place an anvil, a boat, a rail, and a minecart. The Superflat world type is recommended solely to provide deterministic open ground. Use default controls or the corresponding rebound controls.
preconditions: Install and launch the Java Edition release profile for exactly 1.17.1, the first version in the report's explicit Affects versions field. Do not use fix version 23w41a for reproduction.
Use a vanilla client without mods, shaders, resource packs, or datapacks that alter entity rendering or user-interface behavior.
Create a single-player world in Creative Mode so the required items can be obtained without crafting or experience-level preparation.
Have an Anvil, one Oak Boat, one Minecart, and one Rail available. Oak Boat is a concrete boat variant selected because the report does not require a particular wood type.
Leave at least two empty hotbar or inventory slots for the renamed boat and renamed minecart.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start an installation that runs Minecraft Java Edition 1.17.1.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu has loaded under version 1.17.1.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world, set Game Mode to Creative, and optionally select Superflat under More World Options to guarantee open ground. Start the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> World Type: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a Creative Mode world with a flat, unobstructed area nearby.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally before manipulating items.
steps.success_cue: Nearby blocks are rendered, no world-loading screen is present, and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with the inventory control, which is E by default. Use the Search Items tab to locate an Anvil, Oak Boat, Minecart, and Rail, and place one of each into separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the row of nine slots along the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: Search for: Anvil; Oak Boat; Minecart; Rail
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains an Anvil, an Oak Boat, a Minecart, and a Rail.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Esc. Select the Anvil's hotbar slot, point at an open ground block, and use the item by right-clicking to place the anvil.
steps.success_cue: An anvil block is standing on the ground in front of the player.

steps.action: Point at the placed anvil and right-click it to open the anvil interface.
steps.success_cue: The anvil interface is open and shows two input slots, an output slot, and a rename text field.

steps.action: Move the Oak Boat from the hotbar or inventory into the anvil's left input slot.
steps.success_cue: The Oak Boat occupies the left input slot and a boat appears in the output slot.

steps.action: Click the rename text field at the top of the anvil interface. Select or erase the existing item name, then enter the distinct custom name "Boat Test".
steps.success_cue: The anvil output slot contains an Oak Boat whose displayed item name is "Boat Test".

steps.action: Take the renamed Oak Boat from the anvil output slot and place it into an available hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: An Oak Boat named "Boat Test" is present in the hotbar, and the anvil's boat input has been consumed or cleared.

steps.action: While the anvil interface remains open, move the Minecart from the inventory or hotbar into the anvil's left input slot.
steps.success_cue: The Minecart occupies the left input slot and a minecart appears in the output slot.

steps.action: Click the rename text field, select or erase the existing item name, and enter the distinct custom name "Minecart Test".
steps.success_cue: The anvil output slot contains a Minecart whose displayed item name is "Minecart Test".

steps.action: Take the renamed Minecart from the output slot, place it into an available hotbar slot, and close the anvil interface with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view is restored, and the hotbar contains both "Boat Test" and "Minecart Test".

steps.action: Move to an unobstructed patch of ground near the anvil. Ensure there is enough room for the boat and a separate rail block, and keep both placement locations within the same visible, loaded area.
steps.success_cue: Two nearby unobstructed placement locations are available and the surrounding terrain is fully rendered.

steps.action: Select the Oak Boat named "Boat Test" in the hotbar. Point at the first unobstructed ground location and right-click to place the renamed boat. Do not enter the boat.
steps.success_cue: A boat entity is present on the ground and the renamed boat item is no longer held on the cursor or in the selected slot.

steps.action: Select the Rail in the hotbar. Point at the top surface of a solid ground block a short distance from the boat and right-click to place one rail.
steps.success_cue: One rail block is attached to the top of the ground and remains visible near the placed boat.

steps.action: Select the Minecart named "Minecart Test" in the hotbar. Point directly at the placed rail and right-click to place the renamed minecart on it.
steps.exact_input: Select "Minecart Test", then right-click the rail
steps.success_cue: A minecart entity is resting on the rail, while the previously placed boat remains present nearby.

steps.action: Without entering either vehicle, step back far enough to view the boat and minecart clearly. Keep both entities in loaded chunks, close all interfaces, and leave the camera ready for the observation subsystem to inspect each entity from nearby.
steps.success_cue: The renamed boat and renamed minecart are both present in the world, the minecart is on its rail, no interface is open, and the player is positioned close enough to inspect both entities.

stor.handoff_condition: The renamed boat has been placed in the world and the renamed minecart has just been placed on the nearby rail. Both entities are loaded and available for immediate inspection; begin observing their in-world name-tag rendering without entering or removing either vehicle.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, or world type. Creative Mode and a Superflat test world are practical choices for deterministic item acquisition and open placement space, not asserted reproduction requirements.

The report does not specify a boat wood variant or the custom-name text. This plan uses an Oak Boat and the distinct names "Boat Test" and "Minecart Test" so the two renamed entities can be identified reliably.

The wording "Rename a minecart/boat" is grammatically ambiguous, but the following report step explicitly directs the tester to place both a boat and a minecart. This plan therefore renames and places both entity types.
No dedicated-server, multiplayer, operator, command, coordinate, seed, timing, or graphics-setting requirement is given, so the plan uses single-player and does not introduce those conditions.

Comment 12 says the issue was confirmed in 1.18 Pre-release 2, but that version is absent from the report's explicit Affects versions metadata. The affected_versions field follows the explicit metadata list exactly.

source_meta._title: Parity Issue: Ravagers still attack baby villagers in Java Edition

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 21w37a in a newly created vanilla single-player world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled and a non-Peaceful difficulty such as Normal. A Superflat world is recommended to provide clear, level terrain, but the report does not require a particular world type, seed, or coordinates.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected Java Edition snapshot 21w37a. Do not use fix version 1.18 Pre-release 8 for this reproduction.
Use an unmodified vanilla client with no mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter ravager or villager behavior.
Create a new single-player world in Creative mode so the player cannot be harmed and can execute the supplied commands.
Ensure commands/cheats are enabled in the world.
Use Normal difficulty, or another non-Peaceful difficulty, so the ravager remains present.
Perform the test in an open area on solid ground where both summoned entities can be seen and where no unrelated villagers, iron golems, or raiders are close enough to distract the ravager.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the installation profile for snapshot 21w37a, then wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left area of the main menu identifies the running version as 21w37a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and begin creating a new test world. Set the game mode to Creative, ensure commands/cheats are enabled, and set the difficulty to Normal. For a deterministic open testing area, select the Superflat world type if convenient.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is configured for Creative mode with commands available and a non-Peaceful difficulty.

steps.action: Create the world and wait without opening chat or pausing until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world, nearby terrain is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Move to or remain in a clear area on solid ground with enough room to see two large entities. Check that no unrelated villagers, iron golems, pillagers, or other possible ravager targets are nearby.
steps.success_cue: A clear testing area is visible around the player with no nearby entities likely to distract the ravager.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's ravager summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The relative coordinates place the ravager at the player's current position.
steps.success_cue: The command completes successfully and a ravager is visible at or immediately beside the player's position.

steps.action: If entity collision moved the player slightly, stop moving but remain close enough that the ravager stays visible and its chunk remains loaded. Do not attack or otherwise interact with the ravager.
steps.success_cue: The ravager remains present and visible in the loaded testing area, and the game is not paused.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to reopen the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open while the ravager remains loaded nearby.

steps.action: Enter the report's baby-villager summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash and the historical Age NBT value, and press Enter. The relative coordinates place the villager at the player's current position near the ravager.
steps.success_cue: The command completes successfully and a small baby villager is visible at or immediately beside the player and ravager.

steps.action: Do not pause the game, move far away, attack either entity, or issue additional commands. Keep both entities and their surrounding chunk loaded, and allow approximately 2 to 3 seconds of active game time to pass.
steps.success_cue: At least 2 seconds of unpaused game time have elapsed while the ravager and baby villager remained loaded in the same immediate area.

stor.handoff_condition: The ravager and the Age:-25000 baby villager have been summoned close together, and approximately 2 to 3 seconds of unpaused simulation time have elapsed with both entities loaded. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without attacking, moving, pausing, or issuing another command.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, difficulty, world type, seed, coordinates, or whether the test used single-player or a dedicated server. A new single-player Creative Superflat world on Normal difficulty is selected as a minimal, safe, deterministic execution environment rather than as a claimed bug requirement.
The report says to wait 'a couple of seconds'; this plan operationalizes that as approximately 2 to 3 seconds of active, unpaused game time.

Both supplied commands use the same relative coordinates. They are preserved exactly even though summoning both entities at the player's position can cause temporary entity overlap or push the player.
No external verification was needed because the report supplies the affected versions and exact commands required for reproduction.

source_meta._title: Parity Issue: Allays pick up arrow/potion items with other effects than the ones they're holding

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 22w15a in a new single-player Creative-mode world on the integrated server. Use a Superflat world or another open, level area to simplify keeping the allay and dropped item visible. Cheats must be available so the mobGriefing game rule can be confirmed.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected snapshot 22w15a, not the fix version 22w42a or a later release.
Use an unmodded client with no gameplay-changing data packs.
Use a new Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. No particular seed or coordinates are specified by the report.
Keep the test area free of unrelated dropped items and use only one allay.
The mobGriefing game rule must be true; allays cannot collect dropped items when it is false.

Prepare an Arrow of Night Vision as the item handed to the allay and an Arrow of Invisibility as the differently affected tipped arrow dropped for the test. Both must be tipped arrows, not ordinary or spectral arrows.
The instructions refer to default controls. If controls are rebound, use the bindings for Inventory, Use Item/Place Block, Select Hotbar Slot, Chat, and Drop Selected Item.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition snapshot 22w15a, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is responsive and displays 22w15a as the running version.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure cheats are enabled. For a deterministic open test area, select More World Options and cycle World Type to Superflat, then create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a fully loaded Creative-mode world with an open, level area available.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This ensures allays are permitted to collect dropped items.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the mobGriefing game rule is now set to true.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, identified by its compass icon, click the search field, and search for an allay. Hover over the result whose tooltip says Allay Spawn Egg and press 3 to put a stack in hotbar slot 3.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 3 contains an Allay Spawn Egg.

steps.action: While still in the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, replace the search text with the exact item name shown. Locate a tipped-arrow result whose tooltip identifies it as an Arrow of Night Vision, hover over it, and press 1 to put it in hotbar slot 1. Do not select an ordinary Arrow or Spectral Arrow.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains tipped arrows identified by the tooltip as Arrow of Night Vision.

steps.action: Replace the search text with the exact second item name. Locate a tipped-arrow result whose tooltip identifies it as an Arrow of Invisibility, hover over it, and press 2 to put it in hotbar slot 2. The effect must be Invisibility so it is different from the Night Vision arrow in slot 1.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 contains tipped arrows identified by the tooltip as Arrow of Invisibility, while slot 1 still contains Arrow of Night Vision.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory by pressing E or Esc. Press 3 to select the Allay Spawn Egg in hotbar slot 3, then aim at the ground in the open test area.
steps.success_cue: The Allay Spawn Egg is visible in the player's hand and its name appears above the hotbar.

steps.action: Use the selected spawn egg once by right-clicking one ground block. Do not repeatedly click or create additional allays.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one allay is flying near the targeted ground block.

steps.action: Press 1 to select the Arrow of Night Vision stack in hotbar slot 1. Confirm the item name above the hotbar before continuing.
steps.success_cue: Arrow of Night Vision is the active hotbar item and is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Place the crosshair directly over the allay and press the Use Item/Place Block control once, which is right-click by default. Do not attack the allay. The interaction gives one Arrow of Night Vision to it.
steps.success_cue: The allay visibly holds an arrow, begins following the player, and the Arrow of Night Vision stack in slot 1 has decreased by one.

steps.action: Press 2 to select the Arrow of Invisibility stack. Do not use this arrow on the allay; it must be dropped as an item entity.
steps.success_cue: Arrow of Invisibility is the active hotbar item and its name appears above the hotbar, while the allay continues holding the previously given arrow.

steps.action: Move into the open test area and stop when the allay holding the arrow is approximately 2 to 3 blocks away. Face the allay and angle the crosshair slightly downward toward a clear ground block beside it. Ensure no other dropped items are present and do not stand directly on the intended landing point.
steps.success_cue: The arrow-holding allay is nearby, the ground between the player and allay is clear, and the player is ready to throw the selected Arrow of Invisibility toward it.

steps.action: Remain still until the surrounding area is fully rendered, player input is responsive, and the allay is still visible within a few blocks. Keep Arrow of Invisibility selected.
steps.success_cue: The world is responsive, the allay is holding an arrow nearby, and Arrow of Invisibility remains selected.

steps.action: Press the Drop Selected Item control once, Q by default, without holding Ctrl. This drops one Arrow of Invisibility toward the ground beside the allay. Do not walk onto the dropped item or press Q repeatedly.
steps.success_cue: One Arrow of Invisibility item entity has just appeared on the ground near the allay while the allay is still holding the Arrow of Night Vision.

stor.handoff_condition: One Arrow of Invisibility has just been dropped as an item entity within reach of the allay that was previously given an Arrow of Night Vision. The player is not standing on the dropped item. Begin observing the allay's interaction with that dropped arrow immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, seed, or coordinates. A new Creative-mode world and an open Superflat area are practical execution choices, not reported requirements.
The report specifies a Night Vision tipped arrow only as an example and does not name the second effect. Arrow of Invisibility was selected as a deterministic, clearly different tipped-arrow effect.
A comment states that the issue was present in "1.19 Pre-3," but that string is not included in the report's formal Affects versions field, so it was not added to affected_versions.
Comments also mention potions, splash potions, and lingering potions, but the primary Steps to Reproduce use tipped arrows; this plan intentionally reproduces only that supplied arrow variant.

source_meta._title: Frogs don't play their walking animation when they take damage

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 in a single-player Creative-mode world. Use an unobstructed, well-lit area with default or equivalent controls. No particular seed, biome, difficulty, coordinates, server configuration, or graphics setting is specified by the report.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected Java Edition version 1.19, not fix version 23w05a or a later version.

Use a world in which a magma block and a frog can be placed deterministically. Creative mode is recommended because the report does not require Survival mode and Creative inventory provides both items without unrelated crafting or exploration.
Locate a dry, level, unobstructed area where the entire frog can be kept in view.
Ensure surrounding terrain has finished rendering and player movement and inventory interactions respond normally.
Use a single magma block as stated in the report; do not apply NoAI, resistance, invulnerability, or other entity data that could alter the frog's normal damage response or animation state.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select Minecraft: Java Edition version 1.19 and start the game. Do not select 23w05a, because that is listed as the fix version rather than an affected version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 1.19.

steps.action: Create a new single-player Creative-mode world, or load an existing disposable Creative-mode world. For a new world, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, cycle the game mode until it reads Creative, and create the world. Leave the seed and other settings at any values because the report provides no required world configuration.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded world and has access to the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish, then move to a dry, level location with several unobstructed blocks around it. Do not continue while nearby terrain is still appearing or player movement is unresponsive.
steps.exact_input: Use the normal movement controls; defaults are W, A, S, and D.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and there is a clear ground block on which the test block can be placed.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory, select the Search Items tab if necessary, search for “Magma Block,” and move one Magma Block into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: Press E; search for "Magma Block"; left-click or drag Magma Block into a hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Magma Block is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the hotbar slot containing the Magma Block, aim at the top face of a solid ground block in the clear test area, and place exactly one Magma Block.
steps.exact_input: Press E to close the inventory; select the relevant hotbar slot using keys 1-9 or the mouse wheel; right-click the target ground block.
steps.success_cue: One Magma Block is visible in the test area with its top face exposed and no block occupying the space directly above it.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory again, use Search Items to find “Frog Spawn Egg,” and move one Frog Spawn Egg into an empty hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Press E; search for "Frog Spawn Egg"; left-click or drag Frog Spawn Egg into a hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Frog Spawn Egg is present in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing the Frog Spawn Egg.
steps.exact_input: Press E to close the inventory; select the relevant slot using keys 1-9 or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The Frog Spawn Egg is shown as the item held by the player.

steps.action: Stand approximately two to four blocks from the Magma Block with an unobstructed view of its top surface. Aim at the center of the Magma Block's top face. Choose a viewing angle from which the space above the block and the frog's entire body, including its legs, will remain visible without moving the camera after spawning it.
steps.exact_input: Use W, A, S, and D to position the player; move the mouse to aim at the Magma Block's top face.
steps.success_cue: The top face of the Magma Block is within interaction reach and the full space immediately above it is clearly visible.

steps.action: Use the Frog Spawn Egg once on the exposed top face of the Magma Block to spawn a frog directly on the block. Do not repeatedly spawn additional frogs.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once on the top face of the Magma Block while holding the Frog Spawn Egg.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one living frog is visible on top of and in contact with the Magma Block.

steps.action: Immediately release movement and use-item controls, keep the camera centered on the frog's full body, and allow the frog to remain in contact with the Magma Block. Wait only until the first clearly identifiable contact-damage event occurs; a normal damage event may be identified by the frog briefly flashing red and/or producing its hurt sound. Do not attack, push, leash, mount, apply an effect to, or otherwise interact with the frog.
steps.success_cue: The frog is still visible at the Magma Block and has just experienced a contact-damage event without any player attack or other added damage source.

stor.handoff_condition: The frog has been spawned on the single Magma Block, the camera has an unobstructed view of its full body, all player inputs are released, and the frog has just taken contact damage from the Magma Block. Hand control to the observation subsystem while the frog remains available for subsequent damage ticks.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, or server requirement. Creative-mode single player is selected only as a deterministic way to place the required block and frog.

The report says to “summon a frog” but supplies no command or command syntax. This plan uses a Frog Spawn Egg from the Creative inventory to avoid inventing an unreported command while still placing a normal frog directly on the Magma Block.
The phrase “Summon a frog on him” is interpreted as spawning the frog on top of the previously placed Magma Block.

The report does not specify how long to watch. The first identifiable Magma Block damage event is used as the minimum trigger, with the frog left in place for the observation subsystem to inspect subsequent damage ticks if needed.
The frog's variant is not specified, so no particular temperate, warm, or cold variant is required.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-268080:When the projectiles are reflected from the breeze, the projectiles will deflect in the opposite direction in Bedrock, but in Java they will always deflect downward | Relates:inward:MC-268563:Snowballs, eggs, experience bottles, and ender pearls are destroyed instead of being deflected when hitting breezes | Duplicate:inward:MC-268079:Snowballs, eggs and ender pearls break when hitting breeze
source_meta._title: Breezes that are not moving cannot deflect non-arrow and non-trident projectiles

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w03b in a disposable single-player world, with the Update 1.21 experimental features enabled. Use Creative mode, commands/cheats enabled, and any non-Peaceful difficulty. Perform the test in an open, level area with an unobstructed line of sight to one normally functioning Breeze.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and launch the historical Java Edition snapshot 24w03b.
No mods, plugins, or custom data packs are active.
The test world has the Update 1.21 experiment enabled so that the Breeze is available in snapshot 24w03b.
The player is in Creative mode and can execute permission-level-2 commands.
Difficulty is not Peaceful, preventing the summoned hostile mob from immediately disappearing.
The hotbar has at least one available slot for snowballs.
Only one Breeze is used, and its AI is left enabled; do not apply NoAI, place it in a vehicle, or mechanically restrain it.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select the Installations tab, enable snapshot versions in the version filter, and create or select an installation whose version is exactly 24w03b. The official snapshot instructions identify the Installations tab as the place to enable snapshots. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-24w03b?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: An installation profile is selected whose displayed game version is exactly 24w03b, not 24w03a, 24w04a, or the fix version 24w07a.

steps.action: Launch the selected installation. At the main menu, verify that the lower-left version text identifies the running client as Minecraft Java Edition 24w03b.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and visibly reports version 24w03b.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Configure a new disposable world with Game Mode set to Creative, Allow Cheats or Commands enabled, and Difficulty set to Normal. A seed and world type are not specified by the report; the default world type and any seed may be used.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode, commands enabled, and Normal difficulty.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the world-creation Experiments menu, enable the experiment labeled Update 1.21, accept any experimental-feature warning, return to the creation screen, and create the world. Breeze content in 24w03b belongs to the experimental Update 1.21 feature set. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Particles_%28Java_Edition%29?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The world begins loading with the Update 1.21 experiment enabled.

steps.action: After entering the world, wait without issuing commands until nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement and camera input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move and look around normally, and the nearby ground is fully rendered.

steps.action: Move to an open, approximately level location. Stop moving, look horizontally, and point the crosshair toward a clear ground area about five blocks ahead. Ensure there are no walls, trees, other entities, or deep drops between the player and that location.
steps.success_cue: There is a clear, unobstructed line extending at least five blocks forward from the player over level ground.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to open the in-game chat command entry.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and ready to accept a command beginning with a slash.

steps.action: Enter the summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command uses local coordinates to summon one Breeze five blocks in the direction the player is facing. Java summon syntax accepts an entity identifier and position, and the Breeze entity identifier is minecraft:breeze. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3A%E7%94%A8%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4%E6%93%8D%E6%8E%A7%E5%AE%9E%E4%BD%93?variant=zh-hk&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Exactly one living Breeze is visible near the intended point roughly five blocks in front of the player, and no command syntax error appears.

steps.action: Keep a clear line of sight to the Breeze. If it has wandered, reposition carefully so the player is approximately four to eight blocks from it, then release all movement controls. Do not attack it, disable its AI, place it in a boat or minecart, or enclose it with blocks.
steps.success_cue: The Breeze is alive, unobstructed, and close enough to hit directly with a thrown snowball.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open while the Breeze remains present in the loaded area.

steps.action: Enter the give command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This provides sixteen snowballs without requiring crafting or exploration; minecraft:snowball is the namespaced snowball item identifier. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Item_tag_%28Java_Edition%29?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A stack of 16 snowballs is present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command reports successful item delivery rather than a syntax error.

steps.action: Make the snowball stack the active hotbar item. If the stack is already in the nine-slot bar at the bottom of the screen, press the corresponding number key 1 through 9 or scroll to it. If it is only in the inventory, press E, left-click the snowball stack, left-click an empty hotbar slot, close the inventory with E, and select that slot.
steps.success_cue: A snowball is visible in the player's hand, and the selected hotbar slot is outlined around the snowball stack.

steps.action: Release all movement controls and watch the Breeze's body position. Wait for a natural stationary interval in which the Breeze remains on the same spot without walking, sliding, or jumping for at least one continuous second. Rotation in place may be ignored, but do not proceed while its position is changing.
steps.success_cue: The Breeze's position has remained visibly unchanged for at least one continuous second while its normal AI remains enabled.

steps.action: Without moving closer, place the crosshair over the center of the stationary Breeze's body. Confirm immediately before continuing that the Breeze has not begun walking, sliding, or jumping.
